question_text: How does deforestation directly contribute to global warming? / वनों की कटाई सीधे ग्लोबल वार्मिंग में कैसे योगदान देती है?

options.text: It decreases oxygen and increases trapped carbon dioxide in the air. / यह ऑक्सीजन को कम करता है और हवा में फंसी कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड को बढ़ाता है।
Trees release a lot of heat when they are cut down. / पेड़ काटे जाने पर बहुत अधिक गर्मी छोड़ते हैं।
The soil reflects more sunlight back into space. / मिट्टी अधिक धूप को वापस अंतरिक्ष में दर्शाती है।
Fewer trees lead to more rainfall, causing heating. / कम पेड़ों से अधिक वर्षा होती है, जिससे हीटिंग होती है।

explanation: Trees consume carbon dioxide (a greenhouse gas) during photosynthesis. Without them, carbon dioxide accumulates in the atmosphere and traps Earth's heat rays, causing global warming.
distractor_rationale: Option A is correct. Option B is factually wrong. Option C is related to albedo but is not the primary driver of global warming caused by deforestation. Option D is incorrect because fewer trees actually lead to less rainfall.

ai_context.learning_goal: Understand the link between deforestation and global warming via the greenhouse effect.
common_misconceptions: Students often think cutting trees only affects oxygen supply for breathing, ignoring the greenhouse effect of carbon dioxide.
ai_context.hint: Think about what gas plants absorb from the air, and what that gas does to the Earth's temperature.

question_text: Which of the following activities is strictly prohibited in a National Park but might be permitted in a Wildlife Sanctuary under certain conditions? / निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी गतिविधि राष्ट्रीय उद्यान में सख्त वर्जित है लेकिन कुछ शर्तों के तहत वन्यजीव अभयारण्य में अनुमति दी जा सकती है?

options.text: Poaching of wild animals / जंगली जानवरों का शिकार
Grazing of livestock by local tribes / स्थानीय जनजातियों द्वारा पशुओं को चराना
Building a large chemical factory / एक बड़ा रासायनिक कारखाना बनाना
Capturing endangered species for trade / व्यापार के लिए लुप्तप्राय प्रजातियों को पकड़ना

explanation: National Parks are strictly reserved for the betterment of wildlife, and activities like forestry, grazing, or cultivation are not permitted. In contrast, Wildlife Sanctuaries may allow limited human activities like grazing by local communities.
distractor_rationale: Options A, C, and D are illegal and strictly prohibited in BOTH National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries. Only option B highlights the key regulatory difference between the two zones.

ai_context.learning_goal: Differentiate between the rules governing National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries.
common_misconceptions: Students often assume that all protected areas have the exact same strict rules against any human presence.
ai_context.hint: A National Park is like a high-security vault, while a Wildlife Sanctuary is like a protected museum where locals have some limited rights.

question_text: What defines an 'Endemic Species'? / 'स्थानिक प्रजाति (Endemic Species)' को क्या परिभाषित करता है?

options.text: A species that is found in every country in the world. / एक प्रजाति जो दुनिया के हर देश में पाई जाती है।
A species that has gone completely extinct. / एक प्रजाति जो पूरी तरह से विलुप्त हो गई है।
A species found exclusively in one specific geographic area. / एक विशिष्ट भौगोलिक क्षेत्र में विशेष रूप से पाई जाने वाली प्रजाति।
A species that migrates across continents every year. / एक प्रजाति जो हर साल महाद्वीपों में प्रवास करती है।

explanation: Endemic species are those species of plants and animals which are found exclusively in a particular area. They are not naturally found anywhere else.
distractor_rationale: Option A describes cosmopolitan species. Option B describes extinct species. Option D describes migratory species. Option C correctly defines endemic species.

ai_context.learning_goal: Define and identify the concept of endemic species.
ai_context.hint: Think of the word 'exclusive'. If something is only found in your local town and nowhere else in the world, what is it called?

question_text: What is the main purpose of the Red Data Book? / रेड डेटा बुक (Red Data Book) का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?

options.text: To keep a record of all newly discovered planets. / सभी नए खोजे गए ग्रहों का रिकॉर्ड रखना।
To maintain a record of all endangered animals and plants. / सभी लुप्तप्राय जानवरों और पौधों का रिकॉर्ड बनाए रखना।
To list the names of all the National Parks in India. / भारत के सभी राष्ट्रीय उद्यानों के नाम सूचीबद्ध करना।
To record the total population of humans in the world. / दुनिया में इंसानों की कुल आबादी को रिकॉर्ड करना।

explanation: The Red Data Book is the source book which keeps a record of all the endangered animals and plants, helping conservationists track species that are at risk of extinction.
distractor_rationale: Options A, C, and D are incorrect. The Red Data Book specifically focuses on species that are endangered and require conservation efforts.

ai_context.learning_goal: Remember the function and importance of the Red Data Book.
common_misconceptions: Students might think it is a book of dangerous animals because of the color 'red'.
ai_context.hint: Red is often used as a color for warning or danger. What kind of animals are in danger of disappearing forever?

question_text: If a forest was destroyed by a massive wildfire, what is the most effective long-term natural solution to restore the ecosystem? / यदि एक जंगल बड़े पैमाने पर जंगल की आग से नष्ट हो गया था, तो पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र को बहाल करने के लिए सबसे प्रभावी दीर्घकालिक प्राकृतिक समाधान क्या है?

options.text: Building a concrete wall around the burnt area to protect it. / इसे बचाने के लिए जले हुए क्षेत्र के चारों ओर एक कंक्रीट की दीवार बनाना।
Converting the land into an agricultural farm. / भूमि को कृषि फार्म में बदलना।
Reforestation by planting trees of the same species that were destroyed. / नष्ट की गई समान प्रजातियों के पेड़ लगाकर पुनर्वनीकरण (Reforestation)।
Releasing animals into the burnt area immediately. / जले हुए क्षेत्र में जानवरों को तुरंत छोड़ देना।

explanation: Reforestation is restocking of the destroyed forests by planting new trees. The planted trees should generally be of the same species which were found in that forest, in order to restore the original ecosystem.
distractor_rationale: Option A doesn't restore the forest. Option B worsens the loss of the natural ecosystem. Option D is harmful because animals cannot survive without the plants and trees that make up their habitat. Option C is the correct and sustainable solution.

ai_context.learning_goal: Apply the concept of reforestation to a real-world scenario of habitat destruction.
common_misconceptions: Students might think ecosystems can recover simply by adding animals, forgetting that plants are the foundation of the food chain.
ai_context.hint: Animals need food and shelter to survive. What is the foundational step to bring food and shelter back to a destroyed land?
